name: urbanbigdatacentre/ubdc-airbnb
what_it_holds: Containerized, continuously-run scraper (Docker + Django/Celery) that has been collecting DAILY snapshots since 2020 of Airbnb listing property characteristics, booking calendars (day-by-day availability), booking policies, host info, and guest reviews for user-defined geographic areas. Method published/validated in PLOS One 2024 (Enhancing our understanding of short-term rental activity: a daily scrape-based approach for Airbnb listings, PMC10849255) which derives occupancy indicators from calendar-state changes. The actual accumulated dataset (30 UK/Scotland TTWAs, monthly estimates Jun-2021 to Dec-2023) is restricted to UBDC staff (researchdata.gla.ac.uk/2056) but the full scraping/estimation codebase is public on GitHub, so the method (daily calendar-diff -> occupancy/review-count series) is directly reusable against any market.
why_useful: A working, actively-documented (peer-reviewed) daily-calendar-scrape methodology for STR occupancy/availability reconstruction (relevant to gap #2, realised occupancy) and a template for a from-scratch calendar-based occupancy indicator, even though the underlying UK dataset itself is gated. Also directly scrapes airbnb.com, so per repo rules this is catalogued as method only and must not be run without a human ToS decision.
license: unspecified repo license; data access restricted to UBDC staff
last_activity: active research infrastructure as of the PLOS ONE 2024 publication

This is the most rigorous public implementation of exactly the method needed for gap #2 (realised occupancy for STRs from a free/buildable source) and this theme's review-count-as-stays-proxy angle: it operationalizes daily calendar diffing plus review accrual into an occupancy indicator, peer-reviewed, with a working codebase we could point at any of our 123 Inside-Airbnb markets if we wanted independent validation of our own stays index methodology.

Longest-running, still-live daily Airbnb scrape we've found (since 2020, UK-focused), directly targeting reviews/bookings as a stays proxy -- fills gap #1/#2 in kind, but the actual data output is access-restricted so only the method is usable, and it scrapes airbnb.com directly (ToS question, flagged per repo rule 6, not run).

Directly addresses gap #2 (realised occupancy for STRs) and #17 (methods) with a working, non-review-based occupancy/cancellation-estimation pipeline (calendar-diff method) that is an alternative to the Inside Airbnb San Francisco model already in use; also relevant to gap #3 (booking lead time / cancellation, RNPL thesis) since the companion paper explicitly studies cancellation trends via calendar tracking.

A peer-reviewed, published methodology for turning raw Airbnb calendar scrapes into occupancy/activity-level indicators without an AirDNA subscription -- directly relevant to gap #2 as an alternative construction method, and cross-relevant to the team's own Inside-Airbnb calendar work. NOTE: running this against airbnb.com is a scraping decision the CLAUDE.md rules reserve for a human (rule 6) -- catalogue only, do not run.

name: AirBnB_Occupancy
what_it_holds: Implements the classic 'San Francisco Budget & Legislative Analyst's Office' review-based occupancy methodology (review rate 30.5%-72%, midpoint 50%, used to convert Inside Airbnb review counts into estimated bookings, x avg length-of-stay per city, capped at 70% occupancy) and proposes a refinement: filters to multi-listing hosts (20+ properties), 365-day-available, Instant-Book-enabled listings (calendar more likely accurate), then scrapes Airbnb's live calendar API for a subset to validate/calibrate against the review-based estimate. Built on Inside Airbnb listings+reviews as the base dataset. No large committed data files found (methodology/code repo, some scraped calendar snapshots for validation).
why_useful: Directly the 'San Francisco model' / review-to-booking-ratio occupancy estimator named in the theme; addresses gap #2 (realised occupancy for STRs from a free source) — gives a concrete, reproducible formula (review rate x ALOS, city-level) we could re-run on our own 123-market Inside Airbnb panel to get an independent occupancy/nights proxy, and the Instant-Book calendar-accuracy filter is a usable refinement for cross-checking Inside Airbnb calendar-derived occupancy.
geography: Not city-specific in the base method; validation touches at least one city (methodology generalizable to any Inside Airbnb market)
time_coverage: Not specified (uses whatever Inside Airbnb vintage is pulled)
size_hint: small code repo, methodology + some scraped validation data
themes: Airbnb calendar / availability / blocked-night datasets and occupancy-estimation code (San Francisco model, review-to-booking ratios)
why_all: Directly the 'San Francisco model' / review-to-booking-ratio occupancy estimator named in the theme; addresses gap #2 (realised occupancy for STRs from a free source) — gives a concrete, reproducible formula (review rate x ALOS, city-level) we could re-run on our own 123-market Inside Airbnb panel to get an independent occupancy/nights proxy, and the Instant-Book calendar-accuracy filter is a usable refinement for cross-checking Inside Airbnb calendar-derived occupancy.

A clean, inspectable open-source reimplementation of the exact review-rate occupancy methodology already used by Inside Airbnb (which we already lean on) plus an independent calendar-based cross-check idea for calibrating that ratio — useful for validating/adjusting our own occupancy assumptions (gap #2).
